title: Lyten
summary: San Jose company using three-dimensional graphene for lithium-sulfur batteries and composite materials.
bodyHtml:
Lyten manufactures a 3D graphene material and uses it in lithium-sulfur batteries, which avoid nickel and cobalt and can be much lighter than lithium-ion.

The company also sells graphene-enhanced composites and sensors, giving it revenue beyond the battery programme.

Why it matters

  • Lithium-sulfur cells
  • 3D graphene manufacturing
  • Composites and sensors

businessMeaning: Lithium-sulfur has long promised high energy density with cheap materials but suffered from cycle life. Manufacturing the graphene at scale is the differentiator.
investmentLens: Private; a materials platform with a battery option rather than a pure battery bet.
